title: LeanAttention: Hardware-Aware Scalable Attention Mechanism for the Decode-Phase of Transformers
problem: During LLM decode-phase, attention computation suffers critically low GPU SM occupancy because FlashAttention-2 only parallelizes over batch and heads (Nq=1 for decode), leaving most SMs idle; FlashDecoding's fixed-split partitioning causes imbalanced loads and quantization inefficiencies.
motivation: Decode-phase attention constitutes up to 50-60% of total inference time at long contexts; fixed-split partitioning wastes SMs when the number of CTAs is not a multiple of SM count, and the problem worsens for heterogeneous batch context lengths.
method: LeanAttention divides attention work equally across GPU cores using Stream-K, a parallel-processing technique: it breaks the key-value sequence into fixed-size chunks called LeanTiles (each sized optimally for the GPU hardware), distributing them regardless of how attention heads (separate computation paths) are organized. When LeanTiles span head boundaries, their partial results are combined using softmax re-scaling, which is associative—you can compute pieces separately and combine them to get the exact same answer as one complete computation. This keeps GPU cores busy for any sequence length.
key_novelty: LeanAttention proves that softmax re-scaling (the normalization step in attention) is associative, meaning you can compute attention work in arbitrary split pieces and combine them perfectly, enabling full GPU utilization for any context length or batch size.
contributions: Proof and exploitation of associativity of softmax re-scaling as a reduction operator
Stream-K style LeanTile decomposition achieving near-100% SM occupancy for all attention problem sizes
LeanRaggedBatching for heterogeneous context lengths with equal LeanTile distribution
Average 1.73x speedup over FlashDecoding (up to 2.18x at 256k context) on A100; 1.52x average on H100

metrics.speedup: Average 1.73x over FlashDecoding on A100 (max 2.18x at 256k context, 56 heads, BS=2); average 1.52x on H100 (max 2.53x at 64k context); 3.5x at 128k context for head_dim=128
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: More energy-efficient than FlashDecoding at context lengths >128k (lower SM idle time)
metrics.accuracy: Exact attention (no approximation); maintains bit-exact parity with FlashAttention-2
metrics.other: End-to-end: 1.73x speedup on Phi-3 Medium for >16k output tokens

limitations: Reduction overhead grows with splits per head (significant at <4 heads or <1k context); requires input tensor layout (batch, heads, seq, dim) differing from FlashAttention-2; targeted at decode-phase only.
